nodes.statement: Fix an independently grounded binary structural contrast A, independently manipulated binary value contrast V, marker M(A,V), functional outcome Y(A,V), and selected familiar-mineness target F(A,V), while keeping actual bearer, route use, target admission and measurement as distinct application sorts.
nodes.scope: All 16 Boolean tables for each of M, Y and F over four A-by-V cells; not an actual-token admission.
nodes.quantifier: For every Boolean table on the declared four-cell domain.

nodes.statement: Sensitivity to A in both V contexts together with invariance to V at both A poles leaves exactly M=A and M=1-A.
nodes.scope: The declared Boolean marker class only.
nodes.quantifier: For every marker table M(A,V) satisfying both simultaneous constraints.

nodes.statement: Sensitivity of Y to both A and V leaves XOR and XNOR tables, so reversing V at fixed A can flip Y while any structurally specific M remains fixed.
nodes.scope: The declared complete four-cell Boolean outcome class.
nodes.quantifier: For every outcome table satisfying both-axis sensitivity and every C1-admissible marker table.

nodes.statement: Applying structural sensitivity and value invariance to F leaves exactly F=A and F=1-A, which agree on all structural and value relations but reverse the positive familiar-mineness pole.
nodes.scope: The selected familiar-mineness application target in the declared Boolean class, not basal experience.
nodes.quantifier: For every target table satisfying both simultaneous constraints.

nodes.statement: One positive F endpoint selects between the complement pair only if warranted independently of A's label, M's code, Y's value, success, pleasantness and report-defined target construction.
nodes.scope: One admitted actual token and predeclared familiar-mineness target.
nodes.quantifier: For every proposed positive endpoint used to orient F.

nodes.statement: A two-axis application jointly requires same-token actuality, independent A and V grounding, four-cell intervention fidelity, installed route use, predeclared target, separate marker/outcome bridges, one independent endpoint or explicit residual complement, and defeaters.
nodes.quantifier: For every proposed two-axis phenomenal calibration.

nodes.statement: A factorial test is evidence about an actual route and its invariances; it does not install the route, prove same-episode use, identify the complete organization or constitute experience structure.
nodes.scope: Any physical application of the R196 four-cell design.
nodes.quantifier: For every test result used in an R196-style application.

nodes.statement: If V reversal preserves independently grounded A but flips a purportedly structural marker, that marker fails the declared structure-specificity claim; if it leaves M fixed while flipping Y, simple value inheritance is rejected within scope.
nodes.scope: One prospectively declared four-cell application with successful interventions.
nodes.quantifier: For every marker and outcome pair subjected to the complete design.

nodes.statement: Use two-axis reversal to reject value-bound anchors, retain the global phenomenal complement until an independent endpoint is available, and require actual same-instance UCT premises before any familiar-mineness interpretation.
nodes.scope: UCT experience-intelligence-self research; no basal gate, unique owner or assistant-consciousness verdict.
nodes.quantifier: For every future named-target application using the two-axis design.

rules.statement: Enumerate all Boolean marker tables under the simultaneous sensitivity and invariance constraints.
rules.binding: A, V, M and the four declared cells remain fixed across both constraints.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: Non-Boolean, noisy or hidden-variable applications require additional premises and are outside the theorem.

rules.statement: Enumerate outcome tables sensitive to both axes and compare fixed-A value reversals with structurally specific markers.
rules.binding: The same A, V and four cells are used for M and Y; no result is borrowed across experiments.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: A failed intervention or changed A invalidates rather than confirms the dissociation.

rules.statement: Apply the same constraints to F while preserving the existing separation between transported structure and phenomenal naming.
rules.binding: The structural contrast and selected target belong to one proposed application, while remaining distinct sorts.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: Opposite phenomenal orientations preserve every M and Y observation until an independent endpoint is added.

rules.statement: Use the complete value reversal as a negative test of simple value inheritance while refusing to treat test success as actual route use or phenomenal orientation.
rules.binding: The reversal, independently grounded structural contrast, marker and route-use evidence concern the same token and four-cell application.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: Failure to flip Y or preservation failure for A defeats the test; passing it still leaves the target complement open.

rules.statement: Combine the exact dissociation, residual complement and test/use discipline into an eight-field prospective contract.
rules.binding: All fields concern one bearer, interval, signature, route, design and target.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: Missing actuality yields only a table; missing endpoint yields only a value-contamination falsifier.

rules.statement: Place two-axis dissociation inside existing UCT coordinate transport without adding a basal experience gate.
rules.binding: Any positive application retains one actual P/I/K binding and all transport premises simultaneously.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: No individual premise establishes actual application, C1 truth or familiar mineness.

context_links.statement: R196 uses C1 only conditionally and neither proves nor replaces it.
The two-axis contract is not a condition for basal experience.
Structural specificity does not name the positive phenomenal pole.
Factorial evidence does not manufacture same-lineage history or current consumer use.
Value reversal removes one confound while preserving the open phenomenal-direction transfer identified historically in R195.
